subject: Re: MedArc - LLM data use boundary, subprocessors & onboarding next steps
messages:
From: Sophie Lang <sophie.lang@medarchealth.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@medarchealth.com
Date: Tue, 9 Dec 2025 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: MedArc - DPA scope questions (no-training / subprocessors)

Hi Monica,

Thanks again for the demo last week — team was impressed with the latency numbers. We have a couple of items Procurement and Security asked us to confirm before we can move to contracting:

1) No-model-training commitment: we need explicit language that our customer data will not be used to improve models or retained for model training by Redwood. Is that something you can guarantee, and can you point us to the operational proof (logs/snapshots) you provide?
2) Subprocessor roster and onboarding: we need the current subprocessor list and the process for adding a new subprocessor (advance notice, objection window, attestation).
3) Exportability / custody: some of our workflows require SFTP or on-prem export options for transcripts and embeddings. We also require evidence that exports happen only to our designated SFTP endpoint or customer-managed KMS.

Can you send a short checklist and example clause language for the DPA? Procurement would like to see draft language and any supporting runbook or evidence material.

Best,
Sophie Lang
Director, Vendor Risk - MedArc Health
Sophie.Lang@medarchealth.com

---
Attachment: vendor-questionnaire-medarc.xlsx (xlsx) - see tab "security-asks"

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Lang <sophie.lang@medarchealth.com>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 9 Dec 2025 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: MedArc - DPA scope questions (no-training / subprocessors)

Sophie — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers below and I attached a draft DPA annotated for the items you called out (redwood_dpa_draft_v3.pdf). Further detail /ops evidence inlined below.

1) No-model-training commitment
- We can commit to a contractual "no model improvement" clause: Redwood will not use MedArc customer data for model training, tuning, or evaluation without explicit written consent.
- Operational evidence: we provide a per-account flag and weekly attestation export that shows the "training_enabled=false" setting; if you want, we can include a one-time snapshot of the account flag and recent config audit as part of onboarding.

2) Subprocessors
- Attached: current subprocessor_list.csv (names, function, region, data access level).
- Process: 30-day notice for additions; 14-day objection window for enterprise customers; new subprocessors undergo SOC2 review and a data handling attestation.

3) Export / custody options
- We support SFTP push to customer endpoints (encrypted in transit), API bulk export, and an on-prem/private deployment option (VPC package) for residency/KMS control.
- Evidence pack: we can provide a checklist and example SFTP instruction file (sftp-instructions.txt) plus an operations runbook snapshot for audit.

Next steps: Marissa will follow up on contracting language and your Procurement point person. David can provide the KMS/technical export artifacts you need for Security.

If that works, I'll schedule a short call to walk thru the DPA draft and the operational evidence bundle.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0134

Attachments: redwood_dpa_draft_v3.pdf; subprocessor_list.csv; sftp-instructions.txt

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Lang <sophie.lang@medarchealth.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 9 Dec 2025 13:48:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: MedArc - DPA scope questions (no-training / subprocessors)

Sophie, Monica — adding the technical details Security typically requests when they ask for proof of no-training and export safeguards. Short summary here and I can share the evidence bundle on the call.

- No-training enforcement: customer accounts have a per-account control ("learning_consent") implemented in service layer. When set to false, telemetry pipelines and long-term storage are gated; downstream model training buckets are not populated. We can deliver a signed attestation and a recent config snapshot (JSON audit) covering the last 30 days.

- KV/prefix caching: short-lived KV cache (ephemeral) used for session performance is rotated and configured to expire in <24h by default for private accounts. We can show retention config and TTL enforcement logs for a sample timeframe.

- Exports & KMS: exports to SFTP are performed by a scheduled job with destination whitelist. If you opt for customer-managed KMS, we can provide the key-id and a one-off proof-of-possession audit during onboarding. For on-prem Deployments we support BYOK (bring-your-own-key) HSM integration.

- Audit artifacts I can include: 1) config snapshot (redacted) 2) sample export log showing only MedArc destinations 3) attestation template for learning_consent=false.

If you have any regulatory constraints (HIPAA sections, state residency), tell me and I'll prioritize the matching artifacts.

-David
David Kim
Director, Security Engineering, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Lang <sophie.lang@medarchealth.com>, procurement@medarchealth.com
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Dec 2025 10:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: MedArc - DPA scope questions (no-training / subprocessors)

Hi Sophie / Procurement team,

Thanks for surfacing these. I reviewed the DPA draft Monica sent and pulled the specific clause language Procurement can paste into your redlines. I've copied excerpts below for convenience and attached the annotated DPA: redwood_dpa_draft_v3.pdf.

Suggested clause snippets:
- "No Model Improvement": "Provider shall not use Customer Data to train, fine-tune, evaluate, or otherwise improve any machine learning model, model weights, or model-derived features without Customer's prior written consent."
- "Subprocessor Approvals": "Provider shall provide Customer with at least thirty (30) days' advance notice of any new subprocessor and a detailed description of the subprocessor's access and purpose. Customer shall have fourteen (14) days from receipt of notice to object in writing; failure to object shall be deemed consent."
- "Export & Custody": "Provider shall permit Customer-initiated exports of Customer Data via SFTP to Customer-designated endpoints and/or via secure API. Where Customer elects to supply and manage encryption keys, Provider shall accept Customer-managed KMS key IDs and restrict access accordingly."

I recommend we keep the language tight and operationally verifiable (i.e., call out the artifacts we'll hand over during onboarding). If Procurement is comfortable, we can accept redlines inline or propose a two-way SLA exception that covers exports during the pilot.

Action items I propose:
- Monica: schedule 30-min onboarding call (ops + security) — include export/KMS walkthrough.
- David: prepare the attestation pack (config snapshot, sample export logs, learning_consent attestation).
- Sophie / Procurement: share any mandatory clause or internal template you require for vendor DPAs.

Marissa Cole
Sr. Contracts Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

- Please include the subprocessor_list.csv in the package and indicate which subprocessors have access to raw transcript text versus tokenized telemetry.

We can take the call next week — Wed 17th or Thu 18th morning PST both work.

Best,
Sophie
